failure_case.summary: US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.
US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.

llm_output.why_top_candidate_wins: Chile Influenza Activity has the highest aggregate support score (7) and the richest direct links to both the failed target and the mechanism. In the support subgraph it is a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the target signal (signal_us_hosp) (+3) and it has two separate mechanistic links to the mechanism (IMPORTATION_LINK +2 and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF +2). Those combined connections explain both the timing (leading indicator) and a plausible causal pathway (importation / driver) that could cause the model to miss a peak by underpredicting. The other candidates have weaker support: Australia influenza (score 5) lacks an explicit IMPORTATION_LINK to the mechanism in the provided evidence (only LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR + POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF), and Travel Importation Pressure (score 4) lacks a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR link to the target; both therefore provide less direct explanation for a missed peak in US hospitalizations than Chile does.
llm_output.proposed_minimal_edit: Add an importation-forcing term to eq_us_flu_base that takes signal_chile_flu as an external input with an estimated lag parameter. Concretely: create an edge signal_chile_flu --IMPORTATION_FORCE(lag,scale)--> eq_us_flu_base so that recent increases in Chile activity can transiently raise the transmission/importation rate in the US mechanism and thus affect signal_us_hosp.
llm_output.caveat: This recommendation is based solely on the provided graph edges and scores; it assumes the reported links reflect real temporal/causal relationships. Correlation and lead-lag in the graph do not guarantee causation, and the suggested edit should be tested against data (including lag estimation and sensitivity) before being adopted.
